display.purpose: The name on the wallpaper, in orange, on the stacked page.

display-desktop.purpose: One-off: the fluid size of the name on the desktop. Wraps at 8ch.

greeting.purpose: One-off: the greeting beside the portrait in about.md.

prose-heading.purpose: One-off: section headings on the privacy page.

title.purpose: Entry headings such as a job or a project.

brand.purpose: One-off: the brand in the menu bar.

lede.purpose: One-off: the line under the name.

body.purpose: Paragraphs, at most 68ch wide. Also the primary button at weight 600.

meta.purpose: Place and date lines, menu bar text, the Privacy link.

icon-label.purpose: The label under a file icon.

terminal.purpose: Terminal output and the boot log.

prompt-stacked.purpose: One-off: the terminal prompt on the stacked page, 16px so phones do not zoom on focus.

shadows.name: window-rest
shadows.purpose: An open desktop window that is not in front.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The one easing curve: window open and close, press feedback.

motion.name: window-open
motion.purpose: Opacity 0 to 1 and scale 0.96 to 1, growing from the icon that opened the window. Pointer only; instant from the keyboard.

motion.name: window-close
motion.purpose: Opacity to 0 and scale to 0.97. Pointer only; instant from the keyboard.

motion.name: press
motion.purpose: Scale to 0.97 on file icons and the button, 0.95 on window buttons.

motion.name: button-colour
motion.purpose: Background and text colour change on the primary button.

motion.name: boot-lines
motion.purpose: Delays at which the four boot log lines appear, each instantly. Each [ ok ] follows its line by 200, 250 and 800ms.

motion.name: boot-cursor
motion.purpose: Blink of the block cursor on the boot line being worked on.

motion.name: boot-out
motion.purpose: Fade-out of the boot screen. Once per session; any click or key skips it.

motion.name: start-stagger
motion.purpose: On wide desktops the terminal opens first and about.md follows.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: No boot sequence, no scale, no press transitions, no smooth scrolling. Windows still fade.

narrative.overview:
The site is a small operating system, not a page. The wallpaper is flat dark coffee. The content sits in windows of a slightly lighter coffee with a thin outline, and each window is a file with its name in the title bar. Text is cream. Orange is the single accent. The terminal is the darkest window. On small or touch screens, and without JavaScript, the same windows stack into one readable column.

The system shares its orange, its 12px corners and its typefaces (Bricolage Grotesque headings, system sans body) with the owner's other sites. Everything else is quiet: flat fills, 1px lines, two black shadows, and very little motion.
keyCharacteristics: Dark coffee ground, lighter coffee windows, cream text, one orange accent.
1px lines and 12px corners. No gradients, no pills.
Three type voices: Bricolage Grotesque for headings, system sans for reading, mono for filenames and the terminal.
Two layouts from one HTML source: a desktop with draggable windows, and a stacked page.
Motion is short and rare: one boot sequence, then quick window opens and closes.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Orange is the only accent. It marks one thing of each kind: the name, the one button, the front window's icon, the prompt. Everything else is coffee, cream or sand.

rules.name: The Two Oranges Rule
rules.body: Electric Orange is for fills and for text on the wallpaper and in the terminal (5.6:1 and 5.9:1). Text inside a window uses Link Orange, because Electric Orange on Soft Canvas is 4.48:1, just under the 4.5:1 needed for text.

rules.name: The Dark On Orange Rule
rules.body: Text on an orange or cream fill is always Coffee On Orange (5.4:1 on orange). Cream on orange is 3.3:1 and is never used for text.

rules.name: The Darkest Window Rule
rules.body: Only the terminal and the boot screen use Terminal Ground, and only they use amber, green and blue.

rules.name: The Three Voices Rule
rules.body: Bricolage Grotesque is for the name, window titles, entry titles and the "TORRES OS" brand. Mono is for filenames, the terminal, the boot log and inline code. Everything else is system sans.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: The clock and the year column use tabular figures so they do not shift.

rules.name: The Front Window Rule
rules.body: The active window is shown in five ways at once: the deeper shadow, a lighter outline (Stone), a tinted title bar (Soft Canvas, or Terminal Bar), a title in Cream Ink, and an orange label on its file icon. Windows behind it have a Hairline outline, a title bar in their body colour, a Sand title, and a Soft Canvas label on their icon.

rules.name: The Shadows Mean Stacking Rule
rules.body: A shadow says that one thing lies on top of another. Nothing on the stacked page, the menu bar or the buttons has one.

dos: Do keep the wallpaper dark coffee and put content in lighter coffee windows with cream text.
Do keep orange as the single accent, and use Link Orange for text inside a window.
Do put Coffee On Orange text on every orange or cream fill.
Do give every new piece of content its own window with a filename, a file icon and an entry in the terminal, read from the same HTML.
Do use 1px lines: Hairline for outlines and dividers, Stone for the front window.
Do keep hover styles inside `(hover: hover) and (pointer: fine)`.
Do make sure new content also works on the stacked page and without JavaScript.
Do keep window motion at 180ms to open and 120ms to close, instant from the keyboard, with a reduced-motion version that only fades.
donts: Don't use Electric Orange for text inside a window. Use Link Orange.
Don't put cream text on orange.
Don't add a second accent colour. Amber, green and blue belong to the terminal only.
Don't add a light surface or a light theme. Cream is for text, strokes and hover fills.
Don't use gradients, pills or fully round corners.
Don't add shadows on the stacked page, or to buttons and the menu bar.
Don't use mono type outside filenames, the terminal, the boot log and inline code.
Don't add scroll animations, looping animations or a second intro. The boot sequence is the only staged motion.
Don't put cards inside windows. Separate entries with a Hairline rule.
